source.title: FDA Approves Stelara for Pediatric Ulcerative Colitis

sentences.sentence: The US FDA approved Stelara (ustekinumab) for children aged 2 and older with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis, in August 2026.
The US FDA approved Stelara (ustekinumab) injection for paediatric ulcerative colitis in August 2026.
It covers patients aged 2 years and older with moderately to severely active disease.
The FDA says Stelara is the first approved monoclonal antibody not targeting TNF alpha for the two main forms of paediatric inflammatory bowel disease.
This is a US decision; UK availability is decided separately.
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Stelara (ustekinumab) injection for moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis in patients aged 2 years and older.
The FDA's orphan drug database lists the marketing approval date for this use as 28 August 2026.
The FDA says Stelara was approved on 15 April 2026 for moderately to severely active Crohn's disease in patients aged 2 years and older.
The FDA says Stelara is the first approved therapeutic monoclonal antibody that does not target TNF alpha for the two main forms of paediatric inflammatory bowel disease.

The FDA lists the most common adverse reactions in children with ulcerative colitis as nasopharyngitis (a common cold), headache, abdominal pain, influenza, fever, diarrhoea, sinusitis, fatigue and nausea.
Stelara has orphan drug designation for this use.
This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.

source.title: FDA Approves First Gene Therapy for Young Children with Sickle Cell Disease

sentences.sentence: The US FDA approved Casgevy on 1 July 2026 for children aged 2 and older with sickle cell disease, which it calls the first gene therapy for this age group.
The US FDA approved Casgevy (exagamglogene autotemcel) for patients aged 2 years and older on 1 July 2026.
It covers sickle cell disease with recurrent vaso-occlusive crises and transfusion-dependent beta thalassaemia.
The FDA first approved Casgevy and Lyfgenia in December 2023 for patients aged 12 and older.
This is a US decision; UK availability is decided separately.
On 1 July 2026 the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Casgevy (exagamglogene autotemcel) for patients aged 2 years and older.
The FDA says it is the first gene therapy approved for patients aged 2 years and older with sickle cell disease.
The approval covers sickle cell disease with recurrent vaso-occlusive crises, and transfusion-dependent beta thalassaemia.
The FDA first approved Casgevy and Lyfgenia in December 2023 for patients aged 12 and older.
The FDA notes that Casgevy is the first FDA-approved therapy that uses CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing.
Before the Casgevy infusion, patients receive a high-intensity preparatory treatment called myeloablative conditioning.
This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.

source.title: FDA Licenses First-Ever Freeze-Dried Plasma Product in the U.S.

sentences.sentence: The US FDA licensed Ezplaz Freeze Dried Plasma on 29 July 2026, the first freeze-dried plasma product licensed in the US, for adults who need plasma.
The US FDA licensed Ezplaz Freeze Dried Plasma on 29 July 2026.
The FDA says it is the first freeze-dried plasma product licensed in the United States.
Its intended use is transfusion in adults who need plasma and for whom other plasma products are not available.
This is a US decision; UK availability is decided separately.
On 29 July 2026 the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) licensed Ezplaz Freeze Dried Plasma, which it describes as the first freeze-dried plasma product licensed for use in the United States.
Its intended use is transfusion in adult patients who need plasma and for whom other plasma products are not available.
The FDA says Ezplaz is made from a single unit of fresh frozen plasma collected from FDA-licensed blood establishments.
Each kit includes the freeze-dried plasma, a bag of sterile water and transfusion sets.
The FDA says the safety profile of Ezplaz is consistent with other plasma products used for transfusion.
The licence went to Vascular Solutions, LLC, a subsidiary of Teleflex.
Before licensure the FDA had authorised a different product, French FDP, under an emergency use authorisation for military use; the FDA notes it is not an FDA-licensed product.
This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.

source.title: FDA approves first drug to improve functional capacity and symptoms in children with rare inherited heart condition

sentences.sentence: The US FDA approved Camzyos (mavacamten) for children with symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, the first drug for this use in children, on 30 September 2026.
The US FDA approved Camzyos (mavacamten) for children with symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy on 30 September 2026.
The FDA says it is the first treatment to improve functional capacity and symptoms in children with this condition.
Camzyos carries a boxed warning for the risk of heart failure and is available only through a restricted programme.
This is a US decision; UK availability is decided separately.
On 30 September 2026 the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Camzyos (mavacamten) for children with symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
The FDA describes this as the first treatment to improve functional capacity and symptoms in children with the condition.
It describes the condition as inherited and causing a thickened heart muscle, with symptoms that can include shortness of breath, fatigue and an abnormal heart rhythm that can be life-threatening.
In the paediatric study, patients were randomly assigned to Camzyos or placebo, and Camzyos reduced the Valsalva left ventricular outflow tract gradient compared with placebo.
The FDA says adult data showed a similar reduction, and that it expects the drug to help paediatric patients weighing at least 30 kg.
Camzyos carries a boxed warning for the risk of heart failure and is available only through a restricted programme called the Camzyos Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS).
This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.
